quote_text:
Was just saying there, I mean obviously  at any stage of the season when you go  
to the bottom of the league, it's  serious, it's worrying. What does  
it mean at this stage of the season  to go to the bottom of the league? 
Yeah, you said it, everything. It's not  a good situation, but at the same time,  
there's no excuses. There is no time  to feel sorry for yourself. Football  
gives you a chance, a second chance generally, and  we need to grab this second chance. What I mean  
with the second chance is there are still plenty  of games to play, but we cannot wait anymore and  
think, "Okay, we will be okay, we will win this  and this and this," and then we are in April,  
and we are still here. We need to start  winning football matches, and that's how it is.
Somehow, as you said, it's worrying,  it's disappointing, but at the same time,  
it's a kind of reset moment. There's no one  behind us anymore to look at and think, "Okay,  
what happened to their result? What happened  there?" Now, it's everything in front of us. We  
have put ourselves in this position, and it's only  us who will get ourselves out of this position.
Two goals—it seems every time you lose  goals at the minute, they're bad goals,  
aren’t they? Teams aren't having to play  brilliantly to score goals against you. 
Yeah, but that's, again, football logic, how  it works. When you are bottom of the league,  
more likely those kinds of things happen. So  you're not the team that the opponent needs  
to work miracles against to score a goal. And  again, it's our job—my job—to turn it around.
I believe in my players. They are honest players  who are not making excuses about the situation.  
They're not feeling sorry for themselves. Are  they suffering? 100%. If I say maximum confidence,  
of course, it's not there because you're  losing football matches. But at the same time,  
we are a football team. Sometimes you win,  sometimes you lose. And in these moments, you  
need to show what you are, and that's kind of our  moment. We need to show what kind of team we are.
That's why I said it: great belief in our  
players. They will now, in three  days' time, in a big match at home,  
be ready for that. And this is the opportunity  where it all starts—the climbing of the table.
What did you make of the performance today? Football-wise, we knew the opponent would  
come hard from the start, and they  really did. Most of the first half,  
we were a yard off them. We needed to change  our formation a little in the middle of the  
first half because we were planning, or I  was planning, that we could press Hearts  
high and get some turnovers high up the  pitch. But Hearts very cleverly played  
through our press with the long balls, and  they had players to pick up the second balls.
We didn’t have anyone to protect our backline  for those second balls, and then they played  
from that. We were under a lot of pressure.  But then we changed the formation a little bit,  
putting someone to protect our back  four, and we got more players in  
the middle for these second balls. Then  we started to be closer to each other,  
we started to connect some passes, and as we saw  in the second half, we looked like ourselves.
We started to control the game with the ball,  defend with the ball, and keep Hearts out of  
our box. Deservedly, we got the goal to make  it 1-1. But then we had a couple of so-and-so  
moments after the 1-1 situation. We cannot let  the opponent come back that quickly. That killed  
our momentum. Then it was even more difficult to  get back. But football-wise, that's how I feel.
Nicky Clark not available, Kyle  Cameron not available. Next game  
comes on Thursday, so we see where we are.
Are they short-term injuries, just knocks? No, but this is like ice hockey playoffs.  
You don’t give out anything,  because opponents just… yeah.
Okay, thanks. Thank you.
title: Simo Valakari Post Match Press Conference | Hearts 2-1 St Johnstone
